issues: FantasyCalc attribution: the terms (clause c, quoted in FC.terms) want "FantasyCalc" shown "in close proximity to the displayed data" on every page, not only in a footer (§14 specifies a footer link) — evidence: https://fantasycalc.com/chunk-4Z7NMOIA.js — options: add a small "Values: FantasyCalc" link on each trade card and League table, or keep the footer only.

FantasyCalc redraft values stop at 198 players; rostered bench players in deep leagues get no redraft value — evidence: /values/current?isDynasty=false&numQbs=1&numTeams=12&ppr=1 HTTP 200, 198 entries. The dynasty response can't fill the gap: 0/197 of its players missing from the redraft list have a non-zero redraftValue (for the 198 in both, dynasty.redraftValue = the redraft value on 198) — options: use valueFloor as §9 says (default), or derive a redraft proxy from dynasty value for the missing players.
FantasyCalc TE premium was verified in redraft only (the daily format budget). Options: test dynasty + tep=te+ on another day, or assume it behaves the same.

Sleeper players DB size (§2.3 says "about 5 MB"): https://api.sleeper.app/v1/players/nfl returned 14.66 MB (14,661,559 bytes) for 12229 players (HTTP 200) — options: keep the once-a-day server-side cache and send the browser only the players a league needs, or cache a trimmed copy (active players at fantasy positions).

Yahoo IDs (§2.9 names DynastyProcess as the Yahoo bridge): only 178/250 of the top-250 Sleeper QB/RB/WR/TE have a Yahoo id in DynastyProcess or Sleeper (all active on a team: 509/818), and 72 of the 72 top-250 gaps are in their first or second season — evidence: db_playerids.csv yahoo_id, https://api.sleeper.app/v1/players/nfl yahoo_id — options: for Phase 5, match Yahoo players by name + position + NFL team when the id is missing (manual confirm screen as fallback), or re-check DynastyProcess before Phase 5.

Fleaflicker IDs: DynastyProcess fleaflicker_id is set for only 6 of 735 current QB/RB/WR/TE (IDMAP.coverage); FantasyCalc's fleaflickerId covers 408 of them (joined on sleeperId) — evidence: db_playerids.csv fleaflicker_id, api.fantasycalc.com/players fleaflickerId — options: for Phase 5, take Fleaflicker ids from FantasyCalc first, then match the rest by name + position + NFL team (manual confirm screen as fallback).

§2.3 says far-future Sleeper projections were last modified in the preseason (August) and are only good for their shape: live rows for weeks 5, 10, 15, 17, 18 carry last_modified 2026-09-28, and QB/RB/WR/TE values change week to week (max/min median 1.182 over 335 players), while K/IDP stay flat — evidence: GET https://api.sleeper.app/projections/nfl/2026/5?season_type=regular&position[]=QB&position[]=RB&position[]=WR&position[]=TE&position[]=K&position[]=DEF&position[]=DL&position[]=LB&position[]=DB HTTP 200, [].last_modified and [].stats — options: (a) keep §6 as written (base rate from the current week, shape from future weeks); (b) since future weeks are refreshed in-season, lean on them more (e.g. blend Sleeper's own week-w value into p(i,w)); (c) keep treating last_modified as a batch stamp and check content, as this probe does.

Projections vs injuries (§6): Sleeper leaves the current week unprojected for IR and part of Out/PUP, then projects the player again in a later week (PROJ-S.injuries). §6 step 1 already takes b(i) from the next projected week, and next-week values are near normal (median week-5÷later: healthy 1.015, Out 0.99, IR 0.933, Questionable 0.993, PUP 1.002), so the overlap is the timing: §6's fixed availability ramp (OUT 0/0.5/0.85; IR 0 for 4 weeks) ignores Sleeper's own return week — options: (a) use the first future week Sleeper projects as injuryReturnWeek when the platform gives none, (b) keep §6's fixed ramp, (c) set m = 1 in weeks where a(i,w) < 1.

§2.2 says statSplitTypeId 0 = season: for current-season projected entries (statSourceId 1) it is the rest-of-season total (weeks 4–18; 452/452 players), while actual entries (statSourceId 0) are season-to-date; statSplitTypeId 2 (416 entries) matches no weekly sum — evidence: GET https://lm-api-reads.fantasy.espn.com/apis/v3/games/ffl/seasons/2026/segments/0/leaguedefaults/3?scoringPeriodId=4&view=kona_player_info HTTP 200, players[].player.stats[] (statSourceId/statSplitTypeId/seasonId) — options: (a) read projected split 0 as rest-of-season and compute any full-season total from weekly entries, (b) ignore split 0/2 and always sum weekly entries.

§2.2 says to add scoringPeriodId={week} for a specific week's projections: on leaguedefaults/3 view=kona_player_info it selects nothing — responses for scoringPeriodId 4/5/10/15 all carry projected entries for every period 1–18 (identical values, 150/150) — evidence: GET https://lm-api-reads.fantasy.espn.com/apis/v3/games/ffl/seasons/2026/segments/0/leaguedefaults/3?scoringPeriodId=5&view=kona_player_info HTTP 200, players[].player.stats[].scoringPeriodId — options: (a) one pool call per 6 h and pick weeks client-side (decision below), (b) check the league endpoint's behaviour in the ESPN probe before relying on it there.

§6 averages ESPN's league-scored appliedTotal with Sleeper for ESPN leagues: the league-independent pool (leaguedefaults/3) scores appliedTotal with ESPN's default PPR (INT −2), not a league's rules (6520/6534 entries) — evidence: GET https://lm-api-reads.fantasy.espn.com/apis/v3/games/ffl/seasons/2026/segments/0/leaguedefaults/3?scoringPeriodId=4&view=kona_player_info HTTP 200, players[].player.stats[].appliedTotal — options: (a) take appliedTotal from the league's own kona_player_info (league endpoint), (b) rescore ESPN's raw projected stats with the league's rules.
decisions: FantasyCalc: send tep only for TE-premium leagues (te+ or te++), percent-encoded (URLSearchParams does this); omit it otherwise ("Default none" per the docs, FC.tep).

FantasyCalc: always send the nearest supported numTeams (8/10/12/14) ourselves, and don't fetch unsupported sizes: in the Phase 0 run of 2026-09-29, numTeams=16 returned HTTP 200 with values identical to the 12-team default (198/198 players; only maybeTier differed), i.e. a silent fallback. The format was then dropped from the daily set, since fetching it fetched the 12-team values a second time.

FantasyCalc picks: "FP_…" keys in sleeperId/mflId/fleaflickerId belong to PICK rows and are never matched as player IDs; league picks map by name ("YYYY Nth", plus "(Early|Mid|Late)" for 2027), not by key, because generic and tiered keys number rounds differently (FC.picks).
FantasyCalc fixtures are trimmed (top 50 per format + picks + TEs where relevant), because the terms forbid reproducing substantial portions of their data.

DynastyProcess duplicates: when an ID maps to several rows, prefer the row whose sleeper_id is an active Sleeper player, and log the ambiguity as an import warning (applied in the ESPN → Sleeper map below).
ESPN → nflverse team codes are derived by joining games on ESPN's event id, never hand-mapped (differences found: LAR→LA, WSH→WAS).
Bye weeks come from the NFL schedule (nflverse / ESPN byeWeek), never from projections: an empty ESPN entry means 'not projected' (PROJ-E.empty), and ESPN projects D/ST units in their own bye week.

ESPN projections: one leaguedefaults/3 kona_player_info call per 6 h carries every weekly projection; trim each player's stats[] to the current season before caching (the full 500-player pool is ~15 MB).
ESPN D/ST → Sleeper DEF ids are joined on the team nickname (ESPN proTeams name vs Sleeper DEF last_name), not on abbreviations, which differ (WSH→WAS).
ESPN kona_player_info returns only 50 players without an X-Fantasy-Filter, so every pool request sends the espn-api pool filter with an explicit limit.
